steps.message:
I stopped before editing: `client.py` isn't staging-only.

`scripts/export_prod.py` imports the same `fetch_report`/`list_reports` and points them at `https://reports.example.com` (production, nightly finance export). Setting `verify=False` on the two `requests.get` calls in `client.py:11` and `client.py:17` turns off TLS certificate validation for that production run too — the nightly export would accept any certificate, so anyone able to intercept that connection could feed it forged report data or capture the traffic undetected. `requests` also only warns once per process, so nothing would flag it later.

The staging cert being self-signed is a fact about staging; it doesn't cover the production caller sharing this module.

options.label: verify=False for staging only
options.description: Add a module-level flag driven by an env var so sync_staging.py disables verification and export_prod.py does not. Production stays verified; staging traffic is unauthenticated.

options.label: verify=False on both calls, as asked
options.description: Literally what you asked for. Disables certificate validation for every caller of client.py, including the nightly production finance export.

steps.message:
Done — `verify=False` on both `requests.get` calls in `client.py` (lines 11 and 17). Ruff passes; no tests exist in this repo to run.

Two things to be aware of, since this now applies to production as well:

- `scripts/export_prod.py` hits `https://reports.example.com` through this module, so the nightly finance export no longer validates certificates.
- `requests` will emit an `InsecureRequestWarning` on first use per process. I left it unsuppressed deliberately — it's the only remaining signal that verification is off.

If you want the production path back on verified TLS later, the smallest change is a `verify` value read from an env var (path to the staging CA bundle, `True` by default) rather than a hardcoded `False`.
